## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The code uses relative paths, the files sit in the folders the code expects, and the code successfully finds its input and output files on any machine without requiring any edits.

[Supported by: [#55](../../sources.qmd#p55 "Computational reproducibility: a practical framework for data curators"), [#39](../../sources.qmd#p39 "How to make a pie: reproducible research for empirical economics and econometrics"), [#51](../../sources.qmd#p51 "A reproducible data analysis workflow with R Markdown, Git, Make, and Docker"), [#117](../../sources.qmd#p117 "Computational reproducibility of R code supplements on OSF") relative paths, [#93](../../sources.qmd#p93 "Unintended code errors and computational reproducibility") 'code contains relative file paths', [#26](../../sources.qmd#p26 "Facilitating reproducible project management and manuscript development in team science: the projects R package")/[#67](../../sources.qmd#p67 "Tools and recommendations for reproducible teaching") here(), [#23](../../sources.qmd#p23 "Creating and sharing reproducible research code the workflowr way") consistent working directory.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
The code contains hardcoded local paths that cause execution errors, but these paths refer to existing folders/files, so they can be corrected manually or automatically; or the code uses relative paths but some files sit in a different folder than the code expects.

[Supported by: Fixable hard-coded paths: [#99](../../sources.qmd#p99 "Introducing reproducible research standards at the world bank") 'minor and quickly resolvable changes such as adjustments to file paths', [#104](../../sources.qmd#p104 "Reproduce to validate: a comprehensive study on the reproducibility of economics research") path redirection without penalty, [#138](../../sources.qmd#p138 "Reproducibility and robustness of economics and political science research") fixing paths not a failure, [#134](../../sources.qmd#p134 "PaperRepro: automated computational reproducibility assessment for social science papers"), [#105](../../sources.qmd#p105 "Promoting reproducibility and replicability in political science"), [#131](../../sources.qmd#p131 "Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences"), [#74](../../sources.qmd#p74 "Reproducibility as a service"), [#15](../../sources.qmd#p15 "Coding be eR: assessing and improving the reproducibility of R-based research with containR").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
The code contains hardcoded paths that refer to folders/files that do not exist in the replication package. (If the files themselves are missing, this is scored under code/data deposit, not again here.)

[Supported by: [#25](../../sources.qmd#p25 "Toward computational reproducibility: a doctoral student's story of passing the baton") missing files -\> IOError, [#112](../../sources.qmd#p112 "REPRO-bench: can agentic AI systems assess the reproducibility of social science research?") files not in the execution directory, [#125](../../sources.qmd#p125 "A report on 'corruption and Co-optation in autocracy: evidence from Russia'") references to an obsolete subfolder.]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal" title="Show quotes"}
**[#1](../../sources.qmd#p1)** An introduction to docker for reproducible research · *tacit*

> "Docker allows a user to link any directory (such as the working directory for a particular script or project) to the running Docker container." (p. 5)

---

**[#11](../../sources.qmd#p11)** Sciunits: reusable research objects · *tacit*

> "redirecting all system call paths to paths within the special root path of the sandbox container. By redirecting all file requests into the container, the AV execution method fools the application program into believing that it is executing on the original audit-time machine with original file paths." (Sec. III)

---

**[#15](../../sources.qmd#p15)** Coding be eR: assessing and improving the reproducibility of R-based research with containR · *injunctive*

> "using setwd with very specific paths eliminates the possibility of the command executing properly on someone else's computer because different computers almost always have different directory names" (p.17)

---

**[#23](../../sources.qmd#p23)** Creating and sharing reproducible research code the workflowr way · *injunctive*

> It automatically sets the working directory in a consistent manner... This prevents one of the most common failures to reproduce in R—not setting the working directory before running the R script, resulting in incorrectly resolved relative file paths." (p. 5).

---

**[#25](../../sources.qmd#p25)** Toward computational reproducibility: a doctoral student's story of passing the baton · *tacit*

> "some files were missing or located in a different folder which caused IOError messages." (p.689)

---

**[#26](../../sources.qmd#p26)** Facilitating reproducible project management and manuscript development in team science: the projects R package · *tacit*

> "default settings encourage use of the here package to make file paths generalizable; thus, code can successfully access data and other files within the projects folder, no matter where it is located" (p.7)

---

**[#30](../../sources.qmd#p30)** Advancing computational reproducibility in the dataverse data repository platform · *injunctive*

> "Dockerfiles could be susceptible to some of the practices that cause irreproducibility, like the use of absolute (fixed) file paths, which is why Dataverse will encourage its users to use best practices when depositing these files" (p.3, Section 3.2)

---

**[#39](../../sources.qmd#p39)** How to make a pie: reproducible research for empirical economics and econometrics · *injunctive*

> "A first easy-to-implement habit is to use relative paths in programs when calling a function, another program, or a data set" (p. 1149); also invokes "Never type anything that you can obtain from a saved result" (Drukker's dictum) (p. 1149)

---

**[#45](../../sources.qmd#p45)** Toward reusable science with readable code and reproducibility · *tacit*

> "One of the best reproducibility practices is to test research code in a clean environment before publishing it or sharing it online. Doing that helps the researcher (or code depositor) identify common errors such as fixed file paths, missing dependencies, and missing files." (p. 5)

---

**[#51](../../sources.qmd#p51)** A reproducible data analysis workflow with R Markdown, Git, Make, and Docker · *injunctive*

> "it is recommended that all files reside within one folder... and all paths are relative to that folder because absolute paths are specific to a given computer" (p.19)

---

**[#55](../../sources.qmd#p55)** Computational reproducibility: a practical framework for data curators · *injunctive*

> "scripts should use relative paths" (p.7)

---

**[#67](../../sources.qmd#p67)** Tools and recommendations for reproducible teaching · *tacit*

**[#74](../../sources.qmd#p74)** Reproducibility as a service · *injunctive*
